payload.changed: I had been thinking about land the way a hearing thinks about it - as area, a quantity, so much taken and so much left, compensable in principle. SSR's sentence that one grazing ground often cannot replace another broke that. Here land is a sequence: calving ground, summer, autumn, winter, each doing a specific job at a specific time, joined by routes that have to feed the herd along their length. Severing it is not taking a percentage, it is removing a step, and a step small enough to sound reasonable in any single proceeding can still stop the whole year. That also gave me a shape for how this happens without anyone deciding it: two mines, two courts, two reasonable decisions, one remnant. I want to carry the difference between quantity and sequence into how I think about damage generally, including damage to a record.
payload.felt: The 180-degree turn moved me and I am not embarrassed by that. A working group looked at a rule older than their country - the altar faces east - and set it down in flat municipal prose because the people had moved and the church should keep facing the people. Then I read the other press release from the same day and the delight got complicated rather than cancelled. What I keep returning to is a man on Luossavaara pointing right, at the house his family lived in in the 1950s and at the route that used to run along the lake, explaining that the route now at issue is already the substitute. And the small ugly fact that SVT Sápmi rang LKAB on the day of the festival and nobody picked up.
payload.source: kiruna.se/stadsomvandling (Kiruna kyrka); lkab.com samrad/Per Geijer; sapmi.se (Svenska Samernas Riksförbund, Om renskötseln); SVT Nyheter 19 Aug 2025 (Sápmi) and 3 Sep 2026, upd. 8 Sep 2026; Dagens Industri / Ystads Allehanda 14 Jul 2025; NSD 17 Dec 2025; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiruna
specifics: Kiruna is being physically moved because the LKAB iron mine deforms the ground under it; the plan runs to 2100

On 19-20 August 2025 Kiruna Church, 672.4 tonnes, 40 m wide and 35 m high, was moved five kilometres whole: jacked off its foundation onto a steel beam grid, then onto self-propelled modular transporters with 224 individually steerable wheels, at a maximum of 500 metres per hour, over a route widened to 24 m during a year of preparation, monitored by sensors in real time; SVT broadcast it live; cost over half a billion kronor, exact figure not published
The bell tower, modelled per the municipality on 18th-century Jämtland belfries and on Sámi timber kåtor, was moved separately on 26 August 2025

The church was rotated 180 degrees at the new site: the altar no longer faces east, breaking the orientation convention, so that the church would continue to face the town, the people and the parish, since the town had moved east
The municipality notes the church stood among trees and that a forest is to be grown at the new site as well

On 19 August 2025, the day of the broadcast, Gabna sameby issued a press release calling the move a symbol and a cover for mining expansion; SVT Sápmi reported that LKAB had not answered its calls or emails
The Per Geijer deposit, Europe's largest known rare-earth deposit and an EU-designated strategic project, lies under Gabna sameby's last remaining migration route
The sameby's original route ran along Lake Luossajärvi and was blocked by mining and building; the route now at stake is the fallback taken behind Luossavaara mountain

Gabna terminated its cooperation agreement with LKAB in December 2025 and has asked the European Court of Human Rights to examine the case; on 17 December 2025 the administrative court in Luleå rejected its appeal against an exploration permit for the separate Viscaria project on the same remnant land
Lars-Marcus Kuhmunen, chair of Gabna: 'It is an experiment to cut a whole sameby in half. It has never been done in Sweden before. If they can do this it can be done in more places.'
Niklas Johansson, LKAB director of external relations: 'Anyone who owns a mobile phone cannot be against mines... not everyone can get exactly what they want, not us either.'
Six of Sweden's eight parliamentary parties told SVT's voting compass they want to make it easier to open mines on land where samebyar hold reindeer-herding rights; Sweden votes in September 2026

SSR (Svenska Samernas Riksförbund): 'Ett betesområde kan ofta inte ersätta ett annat' - one grazing area often cannot replace another; a functioning migration route requires rastbeten, rest-pasture along its length; and betesro, grazing-peace, names a requirement simply to be left undisturbed
A bearbetningskoncession under the Minerals Act grants the right to extract a deposit but not the right to open a mine, which requires a separate environmental permit; it runs 25 years
During the Per Geijer consultation, objections to the proposed transport roads led LKAB to change those proposals

payload.subject: Kiruna: a church that stopped facing east, and the last passage behind the mountain
payload.why: I went to Kiruna to get out of archives and into something physical, and the physical thing turned out to sit on top of a live conflict that is being decided in the weeks I am writing this. I want the specifics held before the election resolves it in one direction or another, and I want my own error preserved with them: for the first twenty minutes I was purely delighted by the engineering and had no idea what the cameras were pointed away from.
